gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Nordic carves each letter at a single stroke width, tightly closed. Noto Sans Old Hungarian is its opposite: wide-open shapes that stay legible even when shrunk small, which gives the pair its sharpest tension.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-itali: Powerful and ancient, Nordic closes its letters up with a pen-tip stroke that never swells or thins. And Noto Sans Old Italic loosens everything, its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals and its curves left open.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-north: Noto Sans Old North Arabian packs a dense, tall lowercase with terminals flaring outward like tongs. Nordic, by comparison, hunches into closed, brush-dab forms; Noto Sans Old North Arabian is the one that lets the text breathe.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-permi: Nordic's cramped, leaf-fold openings and spaced-apart brush-dab letters give it a weathered, ancient force that stops you at the top of the page. Noto Sans Old Permic then flows along in rounded, open forms.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-sogdi: Noto Sans Old Sogdian reads crisp and tall, its wide mouths holding up when shrunk. Over a long stretch it moves quickly, while Nordic's closed, monoweight letters hold the page back with an ancient weight.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-old-turki: Nordic hits hard with closed letters and a monoweight stroke, spaced like dabs of ink laid far apart. But Noto Sans Old Turkic is the one for steady reading, with open curves and chunky, tall lowercase.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Ancient muscle, modern ease. Nordic does its best work announcing things, drawn as if with one pen tip, while Noto Sans Oriya keeps generous curve gaps and nearly capital-height lowercase for the quieter text below.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-osage: Noto Sans Osage reads in full, inflated bowls and sweeping curves that never close. Nordic's tight, monoweight letters give those curves something to push against, so each font looks more like itself.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Nordic is the one for arresting a glance, with closed, ancient letters spaced like brush dabs. But Noto Sans Osmanya does the quiet work, with easy s turns and a lowercase that towers over its capitals.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hm: Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong has a high-set x-height and rounds that gap like a cracked bangle. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong would look lost if made large, while a small Nordic would clog, its closed forms filling in.
